subject: general
question: What is the name of the first dedicated Indian astronomy mission that is aimed at studying celestial sources in X-ray, optical and UV spectral bands simultaneously?
solution:
The correct answer is __**AstroSat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **AstroSat **is the **first dedicated Indian astronomy mission **aimed at **studying celestial sources **in **X-ray**, **optical **and **UV spectral bands simultaneously**.
 
• The **payloads cover **the **energy bands **of **Ultraviolet **(Near and Far), and **limited optical **and **X-ray regimes **(**0.3 keV to 100keV**). 
 
• **AstroSat **can lift off** a mass of 1515 kg.**
 
• It was **launched **on **September 28, 2015, **into a **650 km orbit **inclined at an angle of **6 deg **to the **equator by PSLV-C30 **from **Satish Dhawan Space Centre**, **Sriharikota**. 
 
• The **minimum useful life **of the **AstroSat mission **is expected to **be 5 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• With the **success of this satellite**, **ISRO has proposed **launching **AstroSat-2 **as a **successor for Astrosat**.
 
• After **injection into Orbit**, the **two solar panels **of AstroSat were automatically **deployed in quick succession**.
 
• The **spacecraft control **center at **Mission Operations Complex **(MOX) of ISRO Telemetry, T**racking and Command Network (ISTRAC**), **Bengaluru **manages the **satellite during its entire mission life**.
